stops.note: the fermented milk of the peoples around Mount Elbrus in the North Caucasus; the word's deeper origin is uncertain (a Turkic word for 'foam' is one guess)
Russian doctors prescribed it from the 1880s; a much-told story has Irina Sakharova obtaining the jealously guarded grains from a Karachay prince in 1908 so Moscow dairies could produce it
described in English from the 1880s; its 'grains' are a living mix of bacteria and yeasts, not cereal

current_meaning: a sour fermented milk drink made with kefir grains
